newsitem.title: UK: Seagate to invest $100 mln in N.Irish plant.
newsitem.headline: Seagate to invest $100 mln in N.Irish plant.

text.p: Seagate Technology Inc said on Tuesday it planned to establish a recording media factory in Limavady, Northern Ireland, involving an investment of $100 million, or 68 million stg.
Northern Ireland's Industrial Development Board (IDB) said it had offered financial assistance of 24.2 million stg towards the project.
The plant is expected to begin production in the second quarter of 1997 and will employ 759 people when fully operational, Seagate said.
The plant will produce nickel-plated aluminium disk substrates for computer hard disk drives.
"We are pleased with the level of success we have achieved at our operations in Northern Ireland," said Alan Shugart, chairman, president and chief executive of Seagate.
"Today's announcement strengthens Seagate's position as a global leader in data technology and we look forward to continued success in the region," he said in a statement.
Seagate already has one factory in Northern Ireland, a plant in Springtown employing 769 people and making thin film heads for disk drives.
